records.title: On Seven Conjectures of Fuchs on Billiard Trajectories in Regular Polygons and Geodesics on the Regular Dodecahedron
records.description:
In a problem contribution (Arnold Math. J. 7 (2021)), D. Fuchs stated seven conjectures on the billiard trajectories in a regular n-gon which join two vertices (short trajectories) and on their n − 2 types A_0, ..., A_{n−3}, on closed trajectories, and on geodesics on the regular dodecahedron. We decide all seven. The tool is the double n-gon: the types are the orbits of saddle connections under an explicit group of affine automorphisms, and they are computed by an angular invariant. Conjecture 2.6 (types of parallel short trajectories) and Conjecture 2.7 (ratios of their lengths) are proved for all n ≥ 4, and Conjecture 2.3 (types of the vertices of a reachable n-gon) for all n ≥ 5. Conjecture 2.5 (reachable points on the two lines through a unitary pair) is true as printed for n = 5 and false for every n ≥ 6; it is proved for all n ≥ 5 with λ² and λ² − 1, λ = 2 cos(π/n), in place of λ + 1 and λ, which are the constants given by the source's own argument for n = 6. Conjecture 2.4 (every reachable point is a vertex of infinitely many reachable n-gons) is false for every n ≥ 5: a reachable point whose type is not A_0 is a vertex of at most one reachable n-gon, and an explicit point is a vertex of none; exactly the points of type A_0 are vertices of infinitely many. Conjecture 3.2 is proved: a short geodesic of type A_0 on the regular dodecahedron never ends at graph distance 2 from its first vertex; its ends are exchanged by a half-turn about the midpoint of an edge, an argument which Athreya, Aulicino and Hooper used for closed saddle connections and Troubetzkoy for the other regular polyhedra. Conjecture 1.7 (after cancellation of common factors, the quotient of the lengths of a closed trajectory and of its preclosed part is never n) is false for every odd n with at least two distinct prime factors; the smallest case is n = 15, for the trajectories parallel to a side. It is true for odd prime powers, and for even n when it is read for the trajectories in general position in their band. These quotients were determined in all periodic directions by Veech (1992), through the monodromy of the covering of the double n-gon by the surface of the billiard; the answer to Conjecture 1.7 follows from his formula by a short computation which is not in his paper. We also give a second derivation of the formula for odd n, and a proof of the counterexample which uses neither surfaces nor homology. For prime n the conjecture was known: this case follows from a theorem of McMullen, for n = 5 from results of Davis, Fuchs and Tabachnikov and of Davis and Lelièvre, and it is also a consequence of Veech's formula. The proofs are elementary. This is an unrefereed note.

Unrefereed preprint released for independent mathematical scrutiny. Publication on Zenodo does not constitute peer review. AI-assisted tools supported research, computation, proof development, and manuscript preparation. The author remains responsible for all claims and the final text.

records.title: A cone-angle proof of Fuchs's labelled length-ratio conjecture
records.description:
This research note gives a cone-angle and classical Veech-cusp proof of Fuchs's Conjecture 2.7: the lengths of source-parallel first-vertex billiard trajectories in every regular n-gon, n≥3, have the canonical labelled sine ratio. The proof includes sides, odd and even double polygons, the physical folding-chart sign, segment-parity reversal, and separate triangular, square and hexagonal marked-lattice cases.

Alper Ferudun's unrefereed preprint of 9 October 2026, DOI10.5281/zenodo.23267641, already states and proves the same nontrivial all-n theorem by angular indices, explicit uniform twists and descent. This note presents a different proof, credits that exact overlapping solution and classical cone-angle/hyperelliptic/Veech machinery, and claims neither a new invariant nor first or exclusive resolution. The repository candidate of 30 September 2026 predates that release, but its substantive folding-chart and physical-reversal correction was recorded on 11 October 2026 at23:57UTC and accepted on 12 October 2026 UTC. We describe the two proof routes as contemporaneous separate developments. The dates do not certify either author's awareness of the other's work or a literally simultaneous publication instant. The corrected proof is not backdated; historical novelty and first or exclusive priority are not certified.

The deposit contains the manuscript PDF and a support archive with standalone LaTeX source, standard-library exact finite controls, an exact pentagon reversal counterexample, recorded outputs, metadata, source locators and priority-search limits. Finite controls support the analytic/geometric proof rather than replace it or prove its imported classical theorems.

AI tools were used extensively in solving, drafting, source comparison, reproduction and independent adversarial checking. This preprint is unrefereed and has not undergone conventional human peer review. The author is responsible for its contents.

records.title: A parity-selected endpoint theorem for the regular dodecahedron
records.description:
This note gives two precise answers associated with Fuchs Conjecture 3.2. The imported bare endpoint-angle condition is false: exactly the two proper face diagonals per initial face and vertex are additional paths and have graph distance two. An explicitly adopted parity-selected convention has a complete unbounded endpoint-exclusion proof through double-pentagon germ symmetry, a physical edge-midpoint half-turn, and a unique-common-neighbor argument. The convention is a supported disambiguation, not an authenticated author correction or uniquely compelled printed reading.

The midpoint and refolding mechanisms are credited to Athreya–Aulicino–Hooper and Troubetzkoy. Alper Ferudun's current contemporaneous preprint, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23267641, contains both the formulation distinction and endpoint theorem, and the public face-word type correction. GitHub records our draft PR creation on 1 October 2026 and DataCite records that related DOI registration on 9 October 2026. These dates do not establish historical exact-byte visibility, firstness, author awareness or independence. On 15 October 2026, the DOI-version files were retrieved successfully and authenticated against record checksums and the previously pinned website hashes; the inspected PDF and source ZIP are byte-identical to the DOI-version files. Uncompleted journal/body-version comparisons remain disclosed. No current openness or guaranteed novelty is claimed.

The deposit includes a four-page research note, standalone LaTeX source and an exact verification package with current optimization-safe guards, meaningful wrong-science controls, distinct independent scientific audits and bounded priority ledgers. records.title: Parallel short trajectories in regular polygons: a type convention and signed angle law
records.description:
This credited research note verifies the signed type law associated with Fuchs Conjecture 2.6 using an explicit segment-parity convention. It proves first-vertex existence and the rule for every n >= 3 and every actually admissible transformed angle, with the required even shift for even n. The unrestricted imported statement combining the rule with a bare type-zero endpoint-angle criterion is false on direct diagonals for every n >= 5; this is distinguished from the source's preceding generic open sectors. The convention is a supported completion, not an authenticated author erratum or uniquely compelled raw-disjunction reading.

Alper Ferudun's version 1.0 preprint of 9 October 2026, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23267641, Definition 1.1, Remark 1.2 and Theorem B, already contains the same nontrivial theorem, parity/diagonal qualification and first-vertex existence. His uniform angular and endpoint-reflection argument, explicit double-surface shears and finite descent substantially overlap the mechanisms here. Veech's exact double-polygon surfaces and shears, Boissy-Lanneau's affine centrality, and earlier pentagon finite-length descent are credited. Neither the theorem, type correction, trivial triangle case, full-affine formulation nor descent is advertised as new.

The fixed original PR191 candidate already contains the common-germ route. GitHub reports PR creation on 1 October 2026, and the current related Zenodo record reports creation on 9 October 2026. These dates and presently retrievable fixed bytes do not establish historical public exact-byte visibility, relative discovery, firstness, awareness or independence.
